Last molecule the budget can score. Ligand 2 is my best at Phi 2.325 and ligand 1 the 4-methyl cyclobutyl version; atom 15 on ligand 1 is the cyclobutane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 13, so I keep that cap and change the azine. I cannot reach the single best cell from this host - that one needs a cyclopropane, which this molecule does not have - so rather than rebuild something I already own I will fill the last open cell on the C4 scan with a carbocyclic cap. A nitrile is the strongest electron-withdrawing group I can put there without adding bulk, and unlike a trifluoromethyl it is linear and light, so it does not wreck lipophilicity; it costs about 24 of TPSA, which on a molecule sitting at LogP 4 is a help rather than a hindrance. Paired with the nitrile-on-oxetane cell I am also scoring this generation, it tells me whether the C4 preference follows electron withdrawal or is specific to halogens, measured on two different caps. Expected product: about 290 Da.
